61:1: God Almighty says: Whatever is in the heavens the seven and whatever is on the earth of creation glorifies God, submitting to Him in divinity and lordship. And He is the Exalted in Might in His punishment of those among them who disobeyed Him, disbelieved in Him, and disobeyed His command. The Wise in His management of them.
61:2: And His statement: O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do? God Almighty says: O you who have believed and believed in God and His Messenger, why do you say what you do not believe in by your actions, for your actions contradict your words.
61:3: It is most hateful to God that you say what you do not do. He says: It is most hateful to your Lord that you say what you do not do. The commentators differed about the reason for which this verse was revealed. Some of them said: It was revealed as a rebuke from God to a group of believers who wished to know the best deeds, so God made them know them. But when they knew, they fell short, so they were rebuked with this verse. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, O you who have believed, why do you say that which you do not do? He said: There were some believers before jihad was made obligatory who would say: We wish that God would show us the most beloved deeds to Him, so that we could do them. So God informed His Prophet that the most beloved deeds to Him are belief in God, without doubt, and jihad against those who disobey Him, who have opposed faith and do not acknowledge it. So when jihad was revealed, some believers disliked that and found it difficult to do so, so God said, O you who have believed, why do you say that which you do not do? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do? Great is hatred in the sight of God that you say what you do not do. He said: There were people who said, By God, if we knew what the most beloved deeds to God are, we would do them. So God revealed to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do? Great is hatred. to His statement, a solid structure. So He guided them to the most beloved deeds to Him. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Juhadah, on the authority of Abu Salih, who said: They said: If we knew which deeds are most beloved and best to God, then the verse was revealed: O you who have believed, shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment? (al-Saff 61:10). They disliked it, so the verse was revealed: O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do? Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, Why do you say what you do not do? up to His statement, well-arranged, in between that, about a group of the Ansar among them, Abdullah ibn Rawahah, they said in a gathering: If we knew which deeds are most beloved to God, we would do them until we die, so God revealed this about them, and Abdullah ibn Rawahah said, I will not cease to be imprisoned in the cause of God until I die, so he was killed as a martyr. Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed to rebuke a group of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, one of whom was boasting about a good deed that he had not done, saying, I did such and such. So God rebuked them for falsely boasting about what they had not done. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, Why do you say what you do not do? He said: It has reached me that it was in jihad. A man would say, I fought and did this, but he had not done this. So God admonished them in that with the most severe admonition. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, O you who have believed, why do you say that which you do not do? He warns them and teaches them as you hear. Great is hatred in the sight of God. And there were men who would report in battle something that they did not do and did not convey, so God admonished them in that with a powerful admonition, saying, O you who have believed, why do you say that which you do not do? until His statement, As if they were a solid structure. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, Why do you say what you do not do? God revealed this about a man who says in battle what he did not do, such as striking, stabbing, and killing. God said, It is most hateful to God that you say what you do not do. Others said: Rather, this is a rebuke from God to a group of hypocrites who promised the believers victory, but they were lying. Who said that? Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement of God, It is most hateful to God that you say what you do not do, they say to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions: If you had gone out, we would have gone out with you and supported you, and we would have been faithful, so he informed them that It is most hateful to God that you say what you do not do. The first of these sayings about the interpretation of the verse is the saying of the one who said: It refers to those who said: If we knew the most beloved deeds to God, we would do them, then they fell short in doing them after they knew. We said: This statement is more appropriate because God, the Most High, addressed the believers with it, saying: O you who have believed. If it had been revealed about the hypocrites, they would not have been named, nor would they have been described as believers. If they had described themselves as doing something they had not done, they would have deliberately lied, and that was not the description of the people. However, in my opinion, they hoped by their saying: If we knew the most beloved deeds to God, we would do them, that if they knew that, they would do it. But when they knew, the strength of some of them weakened from doing what they had hoped to do before knowing, and others became strong and did it, and they had merit and honor. The Arabists differed about the meaning of this and about the reason for placing the word Kabir-e-Maqtan in the accusative case. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: He said, Kabir-e-Maqtan is in the sight of God, meaning, Your hatred is greatly in the sight of God. Then he said, That you say what you do not do means the harm of your speech. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: His statement, O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do? means that the Muslims used to say, If we knew which deeds are most beloved to God, we would do them, even if it cost us our lives and our wealth. Then, on the Day of Uhud, they dismounted from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) until he was wounded and his front tooth was broken. Then he said, Why do you say what you do not do? “Kabir-e-Maqtan is in the sight of God.” Kabir-e-Maqtan means, in is in the nominative case, because kabir is like saying, What a bad man your brother is. His saying, It is greatly hated by God and by those who believe: He implied in greatness a noun that is in the nominative case. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that his saying hated is in the accusative case as an explanation, like the saying of someone who says: This saying is too great.
61:4: God Almighty says to those who say: If we knew the most beloved deeds to God, we would do them until we die. God, O people, loves those who fight in His cause, meaning in His path and religion that He called to, in rows. He means by that that they fight the enemies of God in rows. His saying, As if they were a solid structure, means: They fight in the way of God in a lined up row, as if in their alignment there were walls built in a solid and perfect manner, leaving nothing out. Some of them used to say: It was built with lead. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Indeed, God loves those who fight in His cause in rows as if they were a solid structure. Have you not seen the owner of the structure, how he does not like his structure to differ? Thus, the Blessed and Exalted, His command does not differ. Indeed, God has described the believers in their fighting and described them in their prayer, so adhere to the command of God, for it is a protection for whoever adheres to it. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, Indeed, God loves those who fight in His cause in rows as if they were a solid structure. He said: And those who confirmed their words with their deeds are these. He said: And these did not confirm their words with their deeds when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out, they turned back from him and stayed behind. Some of the people of knowledge used to say: God only said, Indeed, God loves those who fight in His cause in rows to indicate that fighting on foot is more beloved to Him than fighting on horseback, because horsemen do not stand in rows, but rather infantry do. Who said that? Sa`id ibn `Amr al-Sakuni told me: Baqiyah ibn al-Walid told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Maryam, on the authority of Yahya ibn Jabir al-Ta`i, on the authority of Abu Bahriya, who said: They disliked fighting on horses, and preferred fighting on the ground, because of the words of God: Indeed, God loves those who fight in His cause in rows as if they were a solid structure. He said: Abu Bahriya used to say: If you see me turning around in the row, then come to my beard.
61:5: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And remember, O Muhammad, when Moses, son of Imran, said to his people, ‘O my people, why do you harm me while you know the truth? Indeed, I am the Messenger of God to you.’ His statement, So when they deviated, God made their hearts deviate, means: So when they deviated and strayed from the straight path, God made their hearts deviate. He says: God turned their hearts away from it. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Al-Awam told us, he said: Abu Ghalib told us, on the authority of Abu Umamah, regarding his statement, So when they deviated, God caused their hearts to deviate, he said: They are the Khawarij. And God does not guide the wicked people, he said: And God does not guide the people who chose disbelief over faith to attain the truth.
61:6: God Almighty says: And remember also, O Muhammad, when Jesus, son of Mary, said to his people from the Children of Israel, O Children of Israel, I am the Messenger of God to you, confirming what came before me of the Torah which was revealed to Moses and bringing you good tidings “I give you good tidings” of a Messenger to come after me whose name is Ahmad. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Muawiyah ibn Salih told me, on the authority of Saeed ibn Suwayd, on the authority of Abd al-A’la ibn Hilal al-Sulami, on the authority of Arbadh ibn Sariyah, he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “I am written with God as the Seal of the Prophets, and Adam was still kneading in his clay. I will inform you of the beginning of that: the supplication of my father Abraham, and the good report given to Jesus about me, and the vision my mother saw, and so did the mothers of the prophets, they saw that when she gave birth to me, a light came out of her that illuminated the palaces of Ash-Sham.” So when he came to them with clear proofs means: So when Ahmad came to them with clear proofs, which are the evidence that God gave him as proofs of his prophethood, “they said: This is obvious magic” meaning: What he brought was nothing but that I am a magician.
61:7: God Almighty says: And who is more unjust and aggressive than he who invents a lie against God, which is what their speaker said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: He is a magician and when he brought him he was a magician. Likewise, he invents a lie against God while he is being called to Islam. He says: When he is called to enter Islam, he tells a lie against God and invents falsehood about Him. And God does not guide the wrongdoing people. He says: And God does not guide the people who wronged themselves by disbelieving in Him to attain the truth.
61:8: God the Most High says: These people who say about Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, This is an obvious magician, “want to extinguish the light of God with their mouths,” meaning, by saying that he is a magician and that what he brought is magic. And God will perfect His light, meaning, God will declare the truth, make His religion manifest, and support Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, against those who oppose him. That is, the completion of His light. What is meant by light in this passage is Islam. Ibn Zayd used to say: He meant the Qur’an. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, So that they may extinguish the light of God with their mouths, he said: The light of the Qur’an. The reciters differed in their recitation of the Almighty’s saying, And God will perfect His light. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the Kufians, recited it as Muttamm Nooruh in the accusative case. The reciters of Mecca and the majority of the reciters of Kufa recited it as Muttamm without the tanween of Nooruh in the genitive case. These are two well-known recitations with similar meanings, so whichever one the reciter recites, he is correct in our view. And his saying, Even if the disbelievers hate it, means: God will manifest His religion and support His Messenger, even if the disbelievers hate it.
61:9: God Almighty says: God is the One who sent His Messenger Muhammad with guidance and the religion of truth, meaning with the clarification of the truth, and the religion of truth means, and with the religion of God, which is Islam. His statement, To make it prevail over all religions, means: To make His religion, with which He sent His Messenger, prevail over every other religion, and that will be when Jesus, son of Mary, descends, and when the religion becomes one, and there is no religion other than Islam. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu al-Miqdam Thabit ibn Harmaz, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, That He may make it prevail over all religions. He said: The emergence of Jesus, son of Mary. We have already mentioned the disagreement of those who differed regarding the meaning of his statement, That He may make it prevail over all religions. The correct opinion, in our view, regarding that with its reasons, as has passed, is that it is unnecessary to repeat it in this place. And Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja`far told me, saying: Al-Aswad ibn al-`Alaa told us, on the authority of Abu Salamah ibn `Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of `Aishah: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: Night and day will not pass until al-Lat and al-`Uzza are worshipped. `Aishah said: “By God, O Messenger of God, when God revealed the verse, ‘It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to make it prevail over all religions,’ I used to think that this would be complete.” He said: “Indeed, there will be as much of that as God wills, then God will send a pleasant wind, and He will take the souls of those in whose hearts there was the weight of a mustard seed of goodness, and there will remain those in whom there is no good, and they will return to the religion of their fathers.”
61:10: God Almighty says: O you who have believed, shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment? Painful, and that is the punishment of Hell. Then He, may His praise be glorified, explained to us what that transaction is that will save us from the painful punishment.
61:11: He said: You believe in God and His Messenger, Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. If someone were to say: How can it be said, You believe in God and His Messenger, when it was said to them, O you who believe, describing them as believers? The answer to this question is similar to our answer to His statement, O you who believe, believe in God (An-Nisa’: 136). The explanation of this has already been given in its proper place, so there is no need to repeat it. And His statement, And you strive in the cause of God with your wealth and your lives, God Almighty says: And you strive in the religion of God and His way which He has prescribed for you with your wealth and your lives. That is better for you, He says: Your belief in God and His Messenger, and your striving in the cause of God with your wealth and your lives. That is better for you than wasting that and being careless, if you only knew, the harms and benefits of things. And it was mentioned that in Abdullah’s reading believe in God it is in the form of a command, and trade is made clear from His statement, Shall I guide you to a trade that will save you? And it was explained by His statement, You believe in God, and He did not say: that you believe, because when the Arabs explain a noun with a verb, they sometimes confirm in its explanation that that and sometimes omit it, so they say to a man: Would it be good for you to go with us to so-and-so so we can visit him? Would it be good for you to go with so-and-so so we can visit him? That and by putting it forward, and what came in both aspects is his saying, “So let man look at his food. I am” (Abasa 80:24), and inna, so the fat-ha in ana is the language of the one who inserted in yaqoum that from their saying: Would you like it better to stand up? And the kasra in it is the language of the one who throws that from yaqoum, and from it is his saying, “Then see how was the outcome of their plot. Indeed, We destroyed them” (al-Naml 27:51), as we explained. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, O you who have believed, shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you? If God had not made it clear and guided the believers to it, men would have been eager to have knowledge of it, to the point that they would be stingy with it. But God has guided you to it and taught it to you, saying, “You believe in God and His Messenger and strive in the cause of God with your wealth and your lives. That is better for you, if you only knew.” Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, who said: Qatada recited: Shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment? * You believe in God and His Messenger and strive in the cause of God. He said: Praise be to God who made it clear.
61:12: God Almighty says: Your Lord will cover your sins if you do that, and He will pardon you and forgive you. And admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow means: And admit you to orchards beneath whose trees rivers flow. And pleasant dwellings means: And admit you also to pleasant dwellings. In gardens of Eden meaning in gardens of residence, from which there is no departure. And his saying, That is the great victory, means: That is the great salvation from the punishment and horrors of the Hereafter.
61:13: Arabists differed regarding the description of his statement and another. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: The meaning of that is: and another trade. According to this opinion, other must be in the accusative case, in apposition to his statement: Shall I guide you to a trade that will save you from a painful punishment? It may also be possible that it is in the nominative case as a subject. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: It is in the nominative case, meaning that you will have another in this life along with the reward of the hereafter. Then he said: Victory from God, explaining the other. The correct statement regarding this, in my opinion, is the second statement, which is that it means, And for you another which you love, because His statement, Victory from God and an imminent conquest indicates that His statement, And another is in the nominative case. If it had come in the accusative case, it would have been good to make His statement, And another an appositive to His statement, Trade, so the interpretation of the statement would then be, if it had been read in the accusative case, And for another characteristic which you love. So the meaning of the statement, if the matter is as you have described, is: “Shall I guide you to a trade which will save you from a painful punishment? You will believe in God and His Messenger, and He will forgive you your sins and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow. And for you another characteristic besides that in this world which you love: Victory from God for you over your enemies, and an imminent conquest which He will hasten for you.” And give good tidings to the believers. God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And give good tidings, O Muhammad, to the believers of God’s victory for them over their enemy, and an immediate conquest for them.
61:14: And His saying, O you who have believed, be supporters of God. The reciters differed in their recitation of that. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra recited it be supporters of God with the tanween of the supporters, and the majority of the reciters of Kufa recited it by adding the supporters to God. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that they are two well-known readings with correct meanings, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct. The meaning of the statement is: O you who have believed in God and His Messenger, be supporters of God, as Jesus, son of Mary, said to the disciples: Who are my supporters for God? Meaning, who are my supporters among you for God’s support for me? Qatada used to say about this: Bishr told me: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, O you who have believed, be supporters of God, as Jesus, son of Mary, said to the disciples, ‘Who are my supporters for God?’ The disciples said, ‘We are supporters of God.’ He said: God had supporters from among this nation who fought for His Book and His truth. He told us that seventy-two men from the Ansar pledged allegiance to him on the night of Aqaba, and he told us that some of them said, Do you know what you are pledging allegiance to this man for? You are pledging allegiance to fight all of Arabia or they will submit to Islam. He told us that a man said, O Prophet of God, stipulate whatever you wish for your Lord and for yourself. He said, I stipulate for my Lord that you worship Him and do not associate anything with Him, and I stipulate for myself that you protect me from what you protected yourselves and your children from. They said, If we do that, what will we have, O Prophet of God? He said, Victory will be yours in this world and Paradise in the Hereafter. So they did, and God did. Ibn Abd al-A'la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, who said: Qatada recited, Be supporters of God, as Jesus, son of Mary, said to the disciples, ‘Who are my supporters for God?’ He said: That happened, praise be to God. Seventy men came to him and pledged allegiance to him at al-'Aqaba, and they supported him and sheltered him until God made his religion prevail. They said: And no tribe in the heavens was given a name that they had not had before that other than them. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, that all the disciples were from Quraysh 106:Abu Bakr, Umar, Ali, Ja’far, Abu Ubaidah, Uthman ibn Maz’un, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas, Uthman, Talhah ibn Ubayd God, and al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, Who are my helpers to God? He said: Who follows me to God. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Maysarah, on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: Ibn Abbas was asked about the disciples. He said: They were named so because of the whiteness of their clothes. They were fishermen. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, the disciples, that they are the washermen in Nabataean. The washer is called Hawari. We have already explained the meaning of Hawari with its supporting evidence and the disagreements of those who disagreed about it before, so there is no need to repeat it. And His statement, The disciples said, ‘We are supporters of God,’ means: They said, We are supporters of God in what He sent His prophets with of the truth. His statement, So a group of the Children of Israel believed and a group disbelieved, means, Then a group of the Children of Israel believed in Jesus, and a group of them disbelieved in him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When God wanted to raise Jesus to heaven, he went out to his companions, who were in a house, with twelve men from a spring in the house, and his head was dripping with water. He said: There is one among you who will disbelieve in me twelve times after having believed in me. He said: Then he said: Which of you will have my likeness cast upon him so that he will be killed in my place, and be with me in my degree? He said: A young man, one of the youngest of them, stood up. He said: I am. He said to him: Sit down. Then he repeated it to them. A young man stood up and said: I am. He said: Yes, you are that. Then the likeness of Jesus was cast upon him. Jesus was raised from a window in the house to heaven. He said: The Jews came to demand it, and they took his likeness, killed him, and crucified him. Some of them disbelieved in him twelve times after they had believed in him. They split into three groups. One group said: God was among us as long as He willed, then He ascended to heaven. These were the Jacobites. One group said: The Son of God was among us as long as God willed, then He was raised to Him. These were the Nestorians. One group said: The servant and messenger of God was among us as long as God willed, then God raised him to Him. These were the Muslims. The two disbelieving groups conspired against the Muslim woman, so they killed her. Islam remained obliterated until God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then a group of the Children of Israel believed and a group disbelieved. He meant the group of the Children of Israel who disbelieved in the time of Jesus, and the group that believed in the time of Jesus. So We supported those who believed against their enemy, and they became victorious in showing Muhammad’s religion over the religion of the infidels, and they became victorious. And His statement: So We supported those who believed against their enemy means: So We strengthened those who believed from the two groups of the Children of Israel against their enemy, those of them who disbelieved in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, by his confirmation to them that Jesus was the servant and messenger of God, and his denial by those who said he was his god, and those who said he was the son of God, may He be exalted, so they became victorious, so the group of believers became victorious over their enemy, the disbelieving ones among them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Hilali told me: Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: So We supported those who believed against their enemy. He said: We strengthened them. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ibrahim, So a party of the Children of Israel believed and a party disbelieved. He said: When God sent Muhammad, and the confirmation of those who believed in Jesus was revealed, the proof of those who believed in him became clear. He said: Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding his statement, So We supported those who believed against their enemy, and they became dominant. He said: They were supported by Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he believed them and informed them of their argument. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Hisham told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding his statement, And they became apparent, he said: The proof of those who believed in Jesus became apparent by confirming Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as the word of God and His spirit. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And they became apparent, those who believed with Jesus, peace and blessings be upon him.
